The assertions can fail: they are plain String.contains / Int == comparisons with no Optional<Bool>, nothing is mocked, and no threshold was loosened. Ratchet: source-ratchet-selftest.sh exited 0, with sections [4/6] (9 rejects), [5/6] and [6/6] green. I also planted cases in my own scratch copy of the real strings files. These were rejected: %d, %5d, %-3d, %+d, %'d, %*d, %02d, %1$d, %hhd, and a %d on the real notif_discreet_body_fmt key in en only (flagged as both a %d use and a parity mismatch '1:d | 1:ld'). These passed as they should: %ld/%lu, and prose '90% ahora, 100% done, (% Quota)'. Caveats that do not block: (a) %u/%o/%x/%X on an Int also read only 32 bits and the gate does not catch them (a planted %u passed, rc=0). No current key uses them. (b) The space flag '% d' is left out on purpose (see the comment in check-source-ratchets.sh). (c) prose written without a space, such as '90%ahora', is read as a %a specifier. It passes when all three languages match, but a translation that differs from the others could cause a false parity failure. (d) '%*d' consumes one extra argument that the parity index does not count.

The fix is proportionate and follows the repo's rules, including the minimum-fix policy. (1) The Localizable.strings change only swaps %d to %ld, the same edit in all three languages: en.lproj:77,214,253,267,286-287,346-350 and the matching lines in pt-BR and es. (2) The new strings check in scripts/check-source-ratchets.sh:139-214 extends the existing shared script. It does not fork the check into validate.sh or ci.yml, which keeps the 'one definition so they cannot drift' contract stated in its header. It reuses the same patterns as checks 1 and 2: set -euo pipefail, `if ! out=$(perl ...)` for fail-closed on a perl crash, `echo | head -5` and status=1. It fails closed on a missing language file (:158-163) and on a line it cannot parse (:172-175), so nothing is silently read as clean. Block comments are stripped without losing line numbers, so the file:line it reports stays correct. Specifiers are sorted by argument index, so a positional reordering is not a false positive. Leaving out the space flag is deliberate and documented in the comment at :151-153, with a positive control for the prose '90% now (% Quota)' in the self-test [5/6]. \x27 is the only way to put a single quote inside the single-quoted perl script. (3) scripts/source-ratchet-selftest.sh adds 9 rejection cases and 1 acceptance case. expect_reject_strings requires the check's own ✗ message and not just a non-zero exit (:146-160), so a crash does not count as a detection, the same discipline CLAUDE.md asks for ('a gate that cannot fail'). The default STRINGS_DIR=strings-ok export keeps cases [1-3] from depending on the repo's real strings. (4) Tests/AiTaskbarAppTests/IntegerFormatSpecifierTests.swift makes #expect calls only on non-optional Bool values or Int == Int comparisons, so it avoids the vacuous forms banned in section 3. The suite is .serialized and saves and restores L10n.languageOverride with defer, the same pattern as MenuBarTooltipBuilderTests.swift:52-54. The failure message carries language, key and the rendered text. (5) CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md got identical edits, as the cmp check in validate.sh:101 requires. The report says validate exited 0 with 0 warnings and 93.12% coverage. Two cosmetic nits, below the bar for MUDANCAS: reset_confirm_is_64_bit (:57-63) repeats the save/set/restore of languageOverride that render() already wraps, which is justified because it uses the variadic localizedString path of the real call site. The script header still says 'when either check fires' (check-source-ratchets.sh:15) now that there are three checks.

Every touched file ties back to the finding. (1) The three Localizable.strings files each get the same 9 key rewrites %d -> %ld: notif_discreet_body_fmt, service_status_ax_value_fmt, service_status_duration_fmt, reset_confirm_message, credits_local/cloud_msgs_fmt, compare_vs_prev_week/day/month_fmt. en, pt-BR and es are in lockstep, and no other .lproj exists under Sources/AiTaskbarApp/Resources. (2) At every call site the argument is a Swift Int, so %ld is correct everywhere and no Int32 argument was silently widened: NotificationService.swift:158 Int(saturating:), OpenAIResetProtocol.swift:20 availableCount: Int, VendorAnalyticsCardView.swift:9 comparisonOffset: Int, UsageSnapshot.swift:184-185 CreditMessageRange low/high: Int, PopoverContentView.swift:524-526 .count, StatusPanelView.swift:342-346 DurationParts. (3) The new ratchet in scripts/check-source-ratchets.sh is section 3 of the same shared script. Its self-test is extended in scripts/source-ratchet-selftest.sh. .github/workflows/ci.yml:45-46 already calls both scripts, so CI parity holds without editing ci.yml (the comment on ci.yml:43-44 only lists the older checks; cosmetic). (4) validate.sh changes only a comment and the fail message. (5) CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md get the same hard-rule paragraph, and cmp confirms they are byte-identical. (6) Tests/AiTaskbarAppTests/IntegerFormatSpecifierTests.swift is the regression test. No public contract, dependency, host, secret or hot-path cost is introduced; the perl check runs only in validate/CI. No version file was touched, which is correct because auto-tag owns versions.
